correct it, the executor moving or removing a late record, for one blocks every task as an unreadable record does and is never read; (2) rules drift: --task, before each step, compared the rules of main on GitHub with the rule file, every field, with the executor's gh (inv.rules-match-file), and they differ; the question to the owner, who alone changes them; where they could not be compared, a line says why and this branch does not hold (D-185); (3) done: within the current version window, the last round of the review of the result ends its step, as derived.next-round defines the end of a step, or, after the confirmed condition, the record of done that ends the range of fixes follows the narrow round whose acceptance holds (rule.fixes-held-by-tests), and, where the version is compared, the file given is the window's version; the task is done, and the change is merged, its overspend reported with it on that action, of the goal and of the task, by the state of spend the budget question reads: where spend is counted from the logs, the sums from the logs, or with none given the snapshot of spend that the round that ends the task names (rule.ready-after-clean-round, D-169); (4) budget question: the budget with its reserve is exhausted, records of one contribution overlap, a line of the statement's budget cannot be read, or the approved version of the file given has no command of done; the question to the owner, ahead of an open gate; (5) open gate: a gate of derived.next-round after the owner's last approval, a finding not fixable; the question to the owner; (6) no review: no round has read the statement; a review of it; (7) under review: the last round of its review found something; what derived.next-round says for that step; (8) no version: no file is given where the version is compared; give it; (9) changed: the file is not the version approved; a full round of the new version; (10) step: with no round of the result in the window, the executor works under the window's version and records done, or, once its record of done is there, the first full round of the review of the result, numbered after every full round of the step; otherwise what derived.next-round says for the review of the result, read from the start of the window. Every reader of the task, each branch, the acceptance, the end of the task and its overspend, the lines of state and the check, reads the records of the result through one task view, never the task's records whole: its current version is the version of the approval in force, or, while a later round withdraws it, the version last approved, and its window starts at the first of the events at the end of the history that approve that same version, a clean round of the statement or a record of the owner's approval; the rounds of the result and the records of done that name that version on their own Statement-hash: and end after that start are the view's, never a record by its time alone; every other round of the result and record of done of the task ended before that start, in an earlier window, is listed as not read and counts only for the numbers of rounds and for the budget, since one of another version after the start is late and blocks the task; the open gates are not read through the view but from every round of the task, of either step and any version, after the owner's last record of approval; a verdict of acceptance holds only for a record of done of the view as it stood when it was given. --task, --rounds, done.mjs and the check ask it; --task prints it once, on a line NEXT, and every other line of --task and --rounds says a state only; --rounds has no reading of its own: for every task any record names, a round, a record of spend, of done or of the owner's approval, it prints the counts of its rounds by step and then the lines of --task given no file, by the same function, so the two differ only where the file is compared; done.mjs asks it for new work, for which the branch done does not stand, before any refusal of its own, and refuses with that action's text unless it is of kind work: each action carries its kind where it is decided, work (the executor works and may record done), review (a round of the statement's review first), question (the owner is asked, a legacy question of the step too), correct (the records or the file given) or done, and done.mjs never reads the name of a branch: a spent budget refuses a fresh record of done after the task is done too, and with no approval in force the budget question or an open gate is its refusal as in --task. All of them read the records by one function, the commits records name resolved alike. A record is legacy by its time alone, never by the version it names or an approval before it: one before the configuration's reviewRounds.gatesFrom is legacy and reads as it did: its hash, its meaning of not fixable and its gates; it is never late; without the key no record is legacy. Since every round at or after that time names a version, a task none of whose records names one has all its records before it. Whether a task follows branches 6 to 9 is another question, never decided by that time: a task does once any record of it names a version of its statement, a round with Statement-hash:, a record of done or of the owner's approval, or while it has no record; one none of whose records names a version, as one recorded before D-106, skips them. After the confirmed condition and the narrow round, the narrow round's verdict of acceptance, held by these rules as they were when it was given, with findings or without, and the record of done that ends the range of fixes, on another commit after it, are the acceptance of the result together, and that record of done needs no acceptance of its own (rule.fixes-held-by-tests).                                              |

An owner's approval names no commit. Every other round, such as one with a finding on merging or one followed by a later round, and every manual run, proves what it proves without the commit, which a clone made after a rewrite of the history may lack: information, naming each as a record that names a commit this clone does not have, and never a failure. ## Round brief

| Kind     | Term           | ID                           | Type                   | Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

| Entity   | Round brief    | `ent.round-brief`            |                        | The brief of one round of review that round.mjs brief gives: its lines, kept once in ont-briefs/ of the Git directory of the working copy, never in the tree, so that a linked worktree keeps its own; the executor puts them first in the reviewer's brief, and the reviewer's reply begins with them word for word.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Field    | Lines          | `field.round-brief.lines`    | text                   | Task:, Step:, Narrow:, Number:, Statement-hash:, Goal: where the statement names one, from which a reader given no file reads the scope of the budget, held to the configuration's goals (field.task-statement.goal, D-179), Budget-new-input:, Budget-output: and Budget-reserve:, the statement's limits and reserve, each a number or none, the limits of the brief's version, which round.mjs record reads by derived.task-budget for that version, whatever version is approved in force, for a round of the review of a statement that has them, Gate-paths:, its gate paths, which round.mjs record copies into the round (field.review-round.gate-paths, D-185), Commits:, for a round of the result Done:, the record of done it reviews, whose commit Commits: gives, on a round briefed after stagnation Cause:, the SHA-256 of the analysis of the cause given with --cause (field.review-round.cause), and Brief-time:, when the brief was given.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Relation | Round          | `edge.round-brief.round`     | ref ent.review-round   | The round whose record round.mjs record writes from the brief and the reviewer's reply.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Relation | Statement      | `edge.round-brief.statement` | ref ent.task-statement | The version of the statement the round reads, by the SHA-256 of its file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Action   | Brief a round  | `action.brief-round`         |                        | round.mjs brief <task> --step statement --statement FILE, or --step result: refused unless the task's next action, as --task gives it, is a round of that step, or the analysis of the cause after stagnation, after which one follows, and then refused without --cause FILE, the analysis, a file that is not empty, whose text it prints after the lines and whose SHA-256 the brief carries on Cause:; --cause is refused where the next action names no stagnation; of the statement, also while its file is the version the last round with findings read; of the result, unless a record of done is newer than the step's last round, on a commit whose tree differs from the commit of the record of done that round checked, the records of the rounds of that step, their snapshots and the task's records of done aside, so that a commit of a record of a round alone is no new result and corrected records of the process are one; a round for the verdict of acceptance alone, when the last round has none or one the tool refuses, is briefed on the same result. Refused too past the reserve of the goal or of the task: the next action --task gives, with the limits of the version in force, is then the question to the owner (D-179).                                                                                                                                                      |
| Action   | Record a round | `action.record-round`        |                        | round.mjs record <task> --from REPLY --triage FILE: takes the brief, which it removes, and copies its Cause: into the record (field.review-round.cause); refuses a reply whose first lines are not the brief's word for word, or with no brief; reads By:, for a round of the result Condition: and Acceptance: clean, or Acceptance: refused with its reason and a line for each finding of acceptance under it, pass and fail read the same, and the rows of the table of the findings on merging by their class, weight and origin, the reviewer's other columns advice; matches a class to the triage whatever its case and records it as the triage spells it; takes the scope of the budget from the line Goal: of the statement given, or with none given of the task's records, its brief among them (field.task-statement.goal), and refuses a statement given of another version than the brief's; refuses a finding of any weight without the executor's triage, usual path: <step>, not fixable, limitation or later: issues/NNNN.md (rule.executor-triage), a filed finding whose file does not hold its class, and a finding of acceptance filed; where spend is counted from the logs, refuses when no session of the logs holds the brief, and writes the snapshot of spend with the round, which names it; Overspend: only on a round that ends the task with acceptance clean, by that snapshot. |

| Field    | Tests                     | `field.fixes-record.tests` | text optional        | Under Tests:, one line for each class of a fixable finding of that round, word for word, with the file and the name of its test, - class · file · name; the reader of rounds takes the test of a finding from it when the round's record gives none, so that derived.next-round sees the fix held, and the record of the round is never changed. It may be left out only where the record names a valid Issue: (field.fixes-record.issue): a record of fixes holds valid tests, a valid issue or both, never neither, and a valid issue excuses no line under Tests: that is not - class · file · name with a path of the repository (D-186).                                                                                                                            |
| Field    | Issue                     | `field.fixes-record.issue` | text optional        | The line Issue: of a record of fixes, a commit of seven to forty hexadecimal characters, once: the commit of the one issue of verdicts after the narrow round (rule.one-issue-after-narrow), with, under Issue-findings:, the classes of the rows of the table of findings the reviewer of the issue gave, copied by round.mjs fixes --issue <commit> --findings <reply>, and under Filed: the rare ones filed, each with its file. A record with a valid issue may give no line under Tests: (D-186, D-187).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

| Action   | Record the tests of fixes | `action.record-fixes`      |                      | round.mjs fixes <task> --round FILE --from FILE: refuses a class that is not one of a fixable finding of the round word for word, and a file of the repository that does not hold the test named.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

## Test

| Kind      | Term                     | ID                              | Type               | Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Entity    | Test                     | `ent.test`                      |                    | Code that implements checks and starts its title with their IDs.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Relation  | Implements               | `edge.test.checks`              | refs ent.check     | The checks the test implements.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Relation  | In suite                 | `edge.test.suite`               | ref ent.test-suite | The suite the test belongs to.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Rule      | Broken input             | `rule.validator-test-breaks`    |                    | A test of a check that a validator holds, a program that refuses bad files or data, gives it an input that passes and one broken in that check's way, and expects that check's error.                                                                        |
| Invariant | Known checks             | `inv.test-names-known-checks`   |                    | A test names only checks the catalogue has.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Invariant | Only what is built       | `inv.test-only-implemented`     |                    | A test proves only concepts that are implemented.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Invariant | No test of review or run | `inv.no-manual-tested`          |                    | No test implements a check of review or run, the project's or the approach's, or one whose proof is the earlier manual, and no suite names one; the approach's comparison with the oracle, whose test registers it by its tag, is the one exception (D-103). |
| Invariant | Does what it says        | `inv.test-does-what-check-says` |                    | A test does what the check it names says.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

| Check                          | Concepts                        | GIVEN                                                                                                                                                          | WHEN                               | THEN                                                                                                                | Proof  |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| `check.test.unknown-check`     | `inv.test-names-known-checks`   | a test names a check the catalogue does not have                                                                                                               | the check runs                     | it names the check and the suite, and fails                                                                         | auto   |
| `check.test.proves-unbuilt`    | `inv.test-only-implemented`     | a test names a concept, or a check of a concept, that is not implemented                                                                                       | the check runs                     | it names it and fails                                                                                               | auto   |
| `check.test.tags-manual`       | `inv.no-manual-tested`          | tests name a check of review, a check of run, a check whose proof is the earlier `manual` and a check of run of the approach, and a suite names a check of run | the check runs                     | it names each and fails                                                                                             | auto   |
| `check.test.does-what-it-says` | `inv.test-does-what-check-says` | a tagged test                                                                                                                                                  | a reviewer reads it with its check | it sets up GIVEN, does WHEN and asserts THEN                                                                        | review |
| `check.test.validator-breaks`  | `rule.validator-test-breaks`    | a test of a check that a validator holds                                                                                                                       | a reviewer reads it with its check | it runs the validator on an input that passes and on one broken in that check's way, and asserts that check's error | review |

## Test suite

| Kind      | Term                  | ID                                | Type                    | Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Entity    | Test suite            | `ent.test-suite`                  |                         | A kind of test the team runs, such as unit or end-to-end, and the classes it must prove.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Field     | Name                  | `field.test-suite.name`           | text                    | Unique among the suites.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Field     | Covers                | `field.test-suite.cover`          | text                    | The classes whose implemented concepts the suite must prove.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Field     | Judged command        | `field.test-suite.judged-command` | text                    | npm run --silent test:judged: runs the judged suite of the example with the judge JUDGE names, and fails when JUDGE is not set, when JUDGE_VERDICTS, or for the judged checks of views JUDGE_SCREENS, is not set or is inside the repository, and when a test is skipped or does not pass. CI does not run it and npm test no longer runs the judged suite; the executor runs it on changes that touch what it judges and before a release (answer 1042 b, D-187). |
| Relation  | Checks                | `edge.test-suite.checks`          | refs ent.check optional | Checks the suite must implement, such as a key scenario end to end or the checks a judge decides.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Invariant | Unique names          | `inv.suite-names-unique`          |                         | No two suites share a name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Invariant | Not empty             | `inv.suite-not-empty`             |                         | Every suite has test files.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Invariant | Covers its classes    | `inv.suite-covers-classes`        |                         | Every implemented concept of a covered class is proven by a test of the suite.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Invariant | Implements its checks | `inv.suite-implements-checks`     |                         | Every check a suite names, of implemented concepts, is implemented by a test of that suite.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

| Check                                  | Concepts                                                | GIVEN                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | WHEN           | THEN                                                                                                                       | Proof |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `check.test-suite.uncovered-concept`   | `inv.suite-covers-classes`                              | an implemented invariant has no test in the unit suite                                                                                                                                                                                                | the check runs | it names the concept and the suite, and fails                                                                              | auto  |
| `check.test-suite.unimplemented-check` | `inv.suite-implements-checks`, `edge.test-suite.checks` | the end-to-end suite names `check.loan.renew-twice`, and none of its tests implements it                                                                                                                                                              | the check runs | it names the check and the suite, and fails                                                                                | auto  |
| `check.test-suite.duplicate-name`      | `inv.suite-names-unique`                                | two suites are named unit                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | the check runs | it names the suite and fails                                                                                               | auto  |
| `check.test-suite.empty`               | `inv.suite-not-empty`                                   | a suite's directory has no test files                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | the check runs | it names the suite and fails                                                                                               | auto  |
| `check.test-suite.judged-command`      | `field.test-suite.judged-command`                       | the command `test:judged` with no `JUDGE`, with `JUDGE_VERDICTS` missing or inside the repository, with `JUDGE_SCREENS` inside the repository, with a judge that fails a test, and with a judge that passes all; and the scripts `test` and `test:ci` | each runs      | it fails on each of the first four naming why, exits 0 on the last, and neither `test` nor `test:ci` runs the judged suite | auto  |

| --------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Entity    | Ticket                 | `ent.ticket`                   |                          | A slice of the gap: what to build now, within which limits.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

| Relation  | Checks                 | `edge.ticket.checks`           | refs ent.check optional  | The checks of the slice, on the ticket's Checks: line.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Relation  | Depends on             | `edge.ticket.depends-on`       | refs ent.ticket optional | Slices that must be done first.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Derived   | Gap                    | `derived.gap`                  |                          | The work left: target concepts with their checks, automatic checks without a test, known divergences.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Derived   | Slice done             | `derived.slice-done`           |                          | Nothing of the slice left: its concepts implemented, its automatic checks tested, none of the checks it lists waiting for a concept outside it, and no known divergence that names only its concepts.                                                                                                                                   |
| Derived   | Readiness              | `derived.readiness`            |                          | What a target concept waits for: a ticket that takes it, an accepted deferral in force that names it, the owner while only tentative entries name it or an accepted entry naming it names a tentative one, or another target that its definition row or one of its checks names; otherwise it is ready. --gap shows it for each target. |
| Derived   | Next slice             | `derived.next-slice`           |                          | What --next proposes for the next ticket: the ready targets of the first ontology section that has any, the ready targets they depend on, and the checks whose concepts the slice and the code cover.                                                                                                                                   |
| Rule      | No behavior in tickets | `rule.ticket-without-behavior` |                          | A ticket does not describe behavior; behavior is in the check catalogue, written before the ticket.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Rule      | Build what is ready    | `rule.take-ready`              |                          | Work is taken from what --gap marks ready, through a ticket; a target that waits for the owner, a condition or another target is not built ahead of it.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Rule      | Cut when started       | `rule.cut-when-started`        |                          | A ticket is cut when work on its slice starts, not ahead of it, because it takes its concepts out of what --next offers; an agent may cut it from --next, and what the agent may do then is the owner's choice                                                                                                                          |
| Rule      | Closed when done       | `rule.ticket-closed-on-done`   |                          | When --gap with the ticket prints SLICE_DONE and the tests pass, the ticket is closed and kept as the record of the slice                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Rule      | Coordinator cuts       | `rule.coordinator-cuts`        |                          | When several agents work at once, one coordinator cuts all their tickets and commits them to the main branch before they start, since a ticket on another branch takes nothing that the others can see                                                                                                                                  |
| Rule      | One change per slice   | `rule.slice-one-change`        |                          | A slice is one change that a reviewer can read with its own evidence; when what --next proposes is more, it is split along its dependencies and the part the rest depends on is built first                                                                                                                                             |
| Invariant | Names its concepts     | `inv.ticket-has-ids`           |                          | A ticket has an IDs: line.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Invariant | Related checks         | `inv.ticket-checks-related`    |                          | Every check a ticket lists exists and names one of its concepts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Action    | Cut a slice            | `action.cut-slice`             |                          | Take part of the gap and write the ticket with its limits and permissions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

| Check                             | Concepts                                        | GIVEN                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | WHEN                                              | THEN                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Proof  |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |

| `check.ticket.next-slice`         | `derived.next-slice`                            | the example, whose first ready target is `action.set-borrow-limit` in the Member section                                                                                                                                                         | `--next` runs                                     | it prints `NEXT · Member` with `action.set-borrow-limit` on the IDs line and `check.member.set-borrow-limit` on the Checks line; with nothing ready, it says what the targets wait for, and with no target left, what else the gap holds | auto   |
| `check.ticket.no-behavior`        | `rule.ticket-without-behavior`                  | a ticket                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | a reviewer reads it                               | it lists concepts and checks; any behavior it needs is already in the catalogue                                                                                                                                                          | review |
| `check.ticket.take-ready`         | `rule.take-ready`                               | an agent looks for work                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | it takes the next slice                           | the slice holds ready targets only, cut into a ticket from `--next`; a target that waits for the owner is left until the owner answers                                                                                                   | review |
| `check.ticket.cut-when-started`   | `rule.cut-when-started`                         | the tickets open in a project                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | a reviewer reads them                             | each is being worked on now; none was cut ahead to hold concepts for later, and an agent that cut one did only what the owner allows                                                                                                     | review |

## Contract

| Kind      | Term         | ID                     | Type            | Definition                                                                                                                |
| --------- | ------------ | ---------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Entity    | Contract     | `ent.contract`         |                 | A JSON Schema per entity, generated from the types of its fields and relations.                                           |
| Relation  | Describes    | `edge.contract.entity` | ref ent.concept | The entity whose fields and relations the schema describes.                                                               |
| Invariant | Fields typed | `inv.typed-fields`     |                 | Every field and relation has a type from the vocabulary; a view may name the entities it shows; no other kind has a type. |
| Invariant | Current      | `inv.contract-current` |                 | The contract equals what the generator writes now.                                                                        |

| Check                          | Concepts               | GIVEN                                                                                              | WHEN           | THEN                                          | Proof |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `check.contract.untyped-field` | `inv.typed-fields`     | a field row has no type                                                                            | the check runs | it names the field and fails                  | auto  |
| `check.contract.bad-type`      | `inv.typed-fields`     | a field's type is outside the vocabulary, or a reference points at something that is not an entity | the check runs | it names the field and the problem, and fails | auto  |
| `check.contract.stale`         | `inv.contract-current` | the contract was edited by hand, or a type changed without regenerating                            | the check runs | it names the contract file and fails          | auto  |

## Doc section

| Kind      | Term                   | ID                          | Type             | Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Entity    | Doc section            | `ent.doc-section`           |                  | A hand-written section of a page for people, anchored to what it explains.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Field     | Stamp                  | `field.doc-section.stamp`   | text optional    | A short hash of what the section relies on for each concept it explains, the term, type, definition and the notes that name it, as it was when the section was last reread.                                                                                                                                                               |
| Relation  | Explains               | `edge.doc-section.explains` | refs ent.concept | The concepts and checks the section explains.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Relation  | In set                 | `edge.doc-section.set`      | ref ent.doc-set  | The doc set the page belongs to.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Derived   | To reread              | `derived.to-reread`         |                  | A section anchored to a concept whose definition, type or notes changed after its stamp.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Rule      | Every section anchored | `rule.anchor-every-section` |                  | Every section's anchor names what the section explains, the concepts and checks it is about; an empty anchor says it explains no concept, and a section that explains one never has an empty anchor.                                                                                                                                      |
| Rule      | Reread, then stamp     | `rule.reread-then-stamp`    |                  | A section listed as anchored to a changed definition is reread, fixed if needed, and only then stamped.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Rule      | Readers' words         | `rule.readers-words`        |                  | Pages explain in the readers' words; they do not copy definitions, which reference pages restate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Rule      | A guide runs its check | `rule.guide-runs-check`     |                  | A section that explains how to run a check lets someone who has not seen the product run it, and names the check instead of restating its case; where the case needs someone who has not seen something, the reviewer gives a fresh reader, a model without context, only what the case lets it see, and gives the verdict on its result. |
| Invariant | Anchors resolve        | `inv.anchors-resolve`       |                  | Every anchor names IDs of concepts or checks that exist.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Invariant | Every section declares | `inv.section-declared`      |                  | Every heading of the second or third level on a hand-written page of a doc set, outside examples, has an anchor above it with nothing but blank lines between, with IDs or empty.                                                                                                                                                         |

| Check                                        | Concepts                                          | GIVEN                                                                                                                                                                             | WHEN                                                                                                    | THEN                                                                                                                                               | Proof  |

## Ontology tree

| Kind      | Term                      | ID                                | Type             | Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

| Entity    | Ontology tree             | `ent.ontology-tree`               |                  | A page for people that shows the whole ontology as a tree: each entity with the rows of its table by kind, and a table without an entity under its heading. Written by a generator when someone wants to see the ontology, and by the protocol's hook after a merge into main in a clone that names its place; never kept in the repository.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Field     | Place                     | `field.ontology-tree.place`       | text optional    | Where a clone keeps its tree: a path in the clone's own Git configuration, ont.treeOut, never in ont.config.json, so that no path of one machine reaches the repository. Without it, no tree is refreshed and none is reported stale. The place is the file of its name in its directory as the file system resolves that directory, links and .. on the way followed; a place whose directory does not exist is refused. That file is refused with the reason, and nothing is written, when it lies inside a working tree of the repository, any of them, or its Git directory, so that a wrong setting never overwrites a file of the repository; when it is a symbolic link; when it is not a regular file; or when it has more than one link, which may be a file of the repository under another name. The page is written to a new file in that directory and renamed over the place, never into the file that is there, so that a link elsewhere to the old file keeps its bytes. The stale report reads the same file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Field     | Built from                | `field.ontology-tree.built-from`  | text             | What the page was written from, in its mark: one footer in the one form the generator writes, its text saying in the generator's own words what its attributes say, the last element of the page, directly before the </body></html> that ends it with nothing but white space between, with the SHA-256 of the page's bytes before it and of the footer's commit, configuration and date, so that the mark is of the page the generator wrote with that footer, whose footer a person sees; with the commit of HEAD, read once; the path of the configuration from the root of the repository, except outside Git; and the date and time in UTC, to the second, such as 2026-11-20T09:30:00Z. An input's path is the one the configuration gives, never normalised; a .. part on it, or a part of it, the file included, that is a symbolic link or is missing, makes it not the commit's file. The refresh builds the page from the files of that commit, and only when the working tree holds the same at those paths, so its mark is that commit. A page written on demand reads each file of the working tree once, a regular file only, and is marked +working-tree when the bytes read are not the commit's file at the same path inside the repository, or when its path is not the commit's file when the file is read or after; outside Git it is marked no-commit. |
| Relation  | Concepts shown            | `edge.ontology-tree.concepts`     | refs ent.concept | The definition rows the tree shows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Derived   | Stale tree                | `derived.tree-stale`              |                  | The tree at the place is stale when the file is missing, is not a regular file, such as a directory, a named pipe or a symbolic link, which is reported without being opened, or cannot be read; when the page does not end with the mark in the form the generator writes, its attributes and its text, directly before the </body></html> that ends it with nothing but white space between, with the SHA-256 of the page's bytes before it and of the footer's commit, configuration and date, which is no mark whatever text elsewhere on the page, in a comment or an attribute, looks like one, whatever a footer with the right attributes says in other words, and whatever was changed before the footer, one byte included; when the mark has no commit, no configuration or no valid date of that form; when the mark is +working-tree or no-commit, its configuration is not the ont.config.json at the root, or its commit is not the branch main, refs/heads/main. It is reported and blocks nothing, a file that cannot be read included.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Rule      | Only the structure        | `rule.tree-structure-only`        |                  | The tree follows the order of the tables and the configured order of kinds, then the other classes its rows have, as an external ontology's, shows each row by its term with its ID and definition on hover, the entity a field or relation refers to and the entities a view shows, and nothing else. The rows under an entity are its table, not kinds of it. The footer of the page says what it was built from, its commit, configuration and date, and is not part of the tree.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Rule      | Refreshed after a merge   | `rule.tree-refreshed-after-merge` |                  | After a merge into main in a clone that names a place, the protocol's hook writes the tree there from the ont.config.json at the root, built from the files HEAD holds, its commit read once, so that no file of the working tree reaches the page; a file the configuration names that the commit holds as a symbolic link, through one, above the root or not at all is an error of the generator. It writes only when the working tree holds the same files at the paths the configuration gives, never normalised: when the copy of a file it built from is changed, missing or not a regular file, or its path has a .. part or a symbolic link, it writes nothing, the page there stays, and it names the file. A commit is the content its SHA names, never one a local replacement puts in its place. On another branch or without a place it writes nothing and says nothing, before it runs anything else; after a squash merge it writes nothing; when the generator or a file it imports is missing it says so and names the command that restores it; and an error of the generator does not undo the merge. A merge Git ends without the hook, such as a rebase or a resolved conflict, is refreshed by the same command run by hand.                                                                                                                           |
| Rule      | Tree after a server merge | `rule.tree-after-server-merge`    |                  | After each merge through GitHub, the executor brings the clone that serves the tree to the merge: on main, or in a temporary worktree of main when that clone is on another branch, it confirms that ont.treeOut is an absolute path by git config --path, runs git pull --ff-only, confirms that HEAD is the merge commit on origin/main, runs gen-tree.mjs --stale, and when the tree is stale --refresh and --stale again, then confirms that the page's footer names the merge commit, since --stale says nothing of a fresh tree.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

| Derived   | Newer releases       | `derived.newer-releases`          |                   | For a project, the releases its approach clone knows whose verified commit is not an ancestor of the commit of its pin, each read from its tag, with its changes and those of them that change the project's rules, accepted entries that name a concept the project uses; otherwise that there are none, that the pin's commit is not in the clone, or that the clone is not known. A tag that is not a release by the test of inv.release-tagged, the one test the check of the approach asks too, is said and not counted, and then none newer means none among those that can be read. Information that never blocks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Invariant | Releases tagged      | `inv.release-tagged`              |                   | A tag is a release only when it is v and three numbers, annotated, and on the release commit of its entry; every other tag is an invalid tag, said with why. | Action    | Release the protocol | `action.release-protocol`         |                   | In a clean work tree, run the tests and the check on the commit; on a failure, refuse and write nothing; otherwise make the release commit, the child of the verified commit that adds only the entry, check it is that, move the branch to it only from the verified commit, and tag the commit it made. --resume tags a release commit left without its tag, the child of the verified commit that adds exactly its entry, after running the tests and the check again on its parent in a temporary worktree.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
